# Asking Less Often

The fourth pre-release for [#57](https://github.com/timmaurice/bergfex/issues/57). This one changes nothing you see. It cuts down how often the integration asks bergfex for the same page.

## A correction first

`beta.3` said that `www.bergfex.de` refuses requests, full stop. Testing from an affected installation shows it is narrower than that. The refusal is tied to the connection, and it applies only to clients that are not a browser: from that network, curl and Home Assistant got 403 with any user agent, over IPv4 and IPv6, while browsers on other devices in the same network opened the site normally. Why a connection is put in that state is not known. How much it asks is the one part of that the integration controls.

The language switch from `beta.3` still works and is still the way out for a German resort that is refused.

## Fewer requests

On an installation with seventeen entries, a poll sent about seventy requests, around 3,400 a day. Most of them asked for pages another entry had just fetched.

- **The region snow report and the cross-country overview are shared.** Both list every area of a region (or country) at once, but each entry fetched its own copy. The five resorts of Les 3 Vallées asked for the same report five times a poll, and three German trail areas fetched the same overview three times from `www.bergfex.de`. They now share one copy for ten minutes, which is long enough to cover one round of polls and short enough that the new-snow figure never lags behind.
- **Polls running at the same time wait for one another.** All entries poll together, at startup and on each interval after, so they asked for a shared page before the first answer had arrived. The old forecast cache hardly ever helped for that reason: one instance's second poll fetched 59 of its 60 forecast pages again. A page that is already being fetched is now awaited instead of requested again.
- **Forecast pages are kept for three hours instead of ten minutes.** bergfex updates the snow-forecast graphics a few times a day, and the images are named after their content, so a page read three hours ago still points to pictures that exist. This was about half of all requests on its own.

Together these should bring that installation from about seventy requests a poll to about thirty.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. Diagnostics now also report the new shared cache.
